title: Add SLO gate evaluation hooks + required metric tags for optimization config rollouts
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes:
- Rollout controller now emits consistent tenant/model/region/config_version tags on metrics and traces for gating and dashboards.
- Introduces gate evaluation hook interface (error rate + latency) to be wired into safe apply / canary progression.
- Adds default gate thresholds + override plumbing (server-side), with conservative defaults for internal beta.
description: Summary: This PR adds the first-cut SLO gate evaluation hooks used by the optimization config safe-apply rollout controller, and standardizes required metric tags so we can reliably compute gates and annotate dashboards. Motivation: During the rollback gameday + earlier incident review, we saw that gate evaluation was brittle because rollouts were missing consistent labels (tenant/model/region/config_version) and different components emitted slightly different tag keys. This makes it hard to attribute p95/p99 latency and 5xx spikes to a specific optimization config version while a canary is in-flight. What’s in this PR (high level): (1) Gate hook interface: RolloutController now calls a GateEvaluator at each stage boundary (pre-canary, canary step, promote) to decide whether to continue/pause/fail. The evaluator is intentionally side-effect free and returns structured reasons to display in Console. (2) Required metric tags: Added a shared tag helper and enforced tags for any metrics emitted during apply/progress: tenant_id, model_id, region, config_version, rollout_id, and stage (canary|promote|rollback). (3) Default rules: Implemented two initial gate rules: error_rate_5xx (ratio over a rolling window) and latency_p95 (with baseline comparison option), with sane defaults aligned with ADR-safe-apply-gating-signals. Overrides are accepted only from server-side policy (RBAC to come in separate PR). (4) Observability integration: Gate results are emitted as events and metrics (gate_pass/gate_fail with reason_code) so the rollout health dashboard can show “why we paused” alongside latency/error charts. (5) Tests: Unit tests for tag enforcement + evaluator edge cases (no data, sparse traffic, region mismatch) and a small integration test that simulates a canary step failing the error gate and ensures controller transitions to PAUSED with an actionable message. Notes / decisions: - Tag keys are normalized to snake_case to match the existing statsd/prometheus conventions in redwood (previous ad-hoc tags were a mix of configVersion / config_version). - Gate windows are currently fixed at 5m for internal beta; this is intentionally conservative to avoid flapping. We can parameterize once we have more production data and false-positive rates. - The evaluator uses the metrics query client already used by SRE dashboards (no new dependency). The query is wrapped with timeouts and returns UNKNOWN when the data is insufficient; UNKNOWN pauses rollouts rather than promoting. Example tag set (for reference): tenant_id=t_123, model_id=llama-3-70b-instruct, region=us-east-1, config_version=ocv_000142, rollout_id=or_9f3c, stage=canary. Follow-ups (out of scope here): - Console UX wiring to show gate reason codes and a deep link to the exact dashboard panel (Console team). - Additional saturation gates (gpu_util, queue_depth) and p99 latency, plus quality gates for quant profiles (Applied ML + Evals). - RBAC enforcement for gate override policy (Security/Policy). Checklist: - [x] Emit required tags on rollout/apply metrics - [x] Implement gate evaluation hook + default rules - [x] Tests for evaluator + controller transitions - [x] Update internal docs (inline README notes for now; Confluence update in separate doc PR) - [x] Add migration note: tag key normalization (no breaking change, but dashboards should rely on new normalized keys) Related: ENG-4827 (SLO gates), ENG-4824 (canary rollout controller).

conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): The hook points look right, but I’m concerned about defaulting UNKNOWN -> PASS. For safety we should pause (or fail) if we can’t query metrics reliably. Also, can we ensure the tag keys exactly match what the dashboard expects? Allison Grant (review): +1 on tag consistency. Please also add rollout_id and stage to every emitted metric; otherwise the panels can’t separate concurrent rollouts. Noah Patel (review): Runtime emits config_version today in some places as configVersion. We should normalize at the boundaries; make sure we’re not breaking existing parsing. Jordan Lee (review): For overrides: please don’t accept arbitrary client-provided thresholds yet; keep it server-side until RBAC is in. Also, return structured reason codes so Console can show a stable message. Benji Okafor (author): Updated evaluator behavior: UNKNOWN now causes controller to PAUSE and returns reason_code=INSUFFICIENT_DATA with a human message. Tag helper now enforces tenant_id/model_id/region/config_version/rollout_id/stage, and I added tests that fail if any are missing. Also removed client-provided overrides; config is loaded from server defaults only. Sean Gallagher (follow-up): Looks good. One nit: the latency rule baseline compare uses median of last 30m; can we cap queries and add timeouts? Benji Okafor: Added 2s timeout on metrics queries and bounded lookback to 30m max; when timeouts occur we pause and emit reason_code=METRICS_QUERY_TIMEOUT. Allison Grant: Please add a gate_fail metric with reason_code tag; this helps alerting. Benji Okafor: Done: gate_result{result=pass|fail|unknown, reason_code=...} and a dedicated counter gate_fail_total with required tags. Jordan Lee: Thanks for removing client overrides. Approved. Sean Gallagher: Approved once CI is green. Noah Patel: Approved; normalization helper is a good step. Merge: Squashed after CI passed; linked follow-up tasks to add saturation gates + Console deep links.
